thread:
maria: Heads up — seeing a gradual rise in NVMe remap_count and partial badblock remaps across a subset of ephemeral drives in us-west2. Started 02:15 UTC, now 0.9% of attach attempts for GPU batches hit transient I/O errors and slow attach times.

devops-bot: ALERT: nvme.remap_rate(us-west2) >= 0.7% for 10m — investigate (rule: nvme-wear-detect).

ajay: Can you paste the latest smartlog and iostat snapshot? Need to know if it's thermal/wear or firmware.

maria: Quick dump below (truncated):

```
$ smartctl -a /dev/nvme0n1
Device Model: ACME-NVMe-3XX
SMART overall-health self-assessment test result: PASSED
Data Units Written: 1,234,567
Percentage Used: 68%
Media and Data Integrity Errors: 12
Current Temp: 47C

$ iostat -x 1 3
avg-cpu:  2.1 us  0.4 sy  0.0 id
Device: tps    kB_read/s kB_wrtn/s  await r_await w_await svctm
nvme0n1: 45.3  12.1     204.3    18.7  4.2    19.1    0.21
```

maria: Media errors concentrated on a handful of nodes (node ids: gnode-57a, gnode-57b, gnode-57c). I think remap_count spike + higher await on nvme0n1 correlates with GPU batch attach slowdowns.

leo: Are these nodes backing critical dedicated pools or ephemeral batch-only pools? We should avoid mass-retire if they're only in low-tier pools.

maria: They sit in ephemeral batch pool (preemptible-like). Attach failures cause retries which push other nodes to overcommit.

sophia: Short term mitigation: increase attach retry backoff and shrink batch concurrency for the next 2 hours to bleed load. Long term: we should proactively retire drives that cross media_errors > 5 and pct_used > 65%.

ajay: Agree. Cost tradeoff: retiring 3 nodes will reduce available GPU slots by ~6% during peak; forcing batch windows will increase latency and cost per inference. Which is cheaper?

leo: Quick cost calc: 3-node retirement cost = ~3 * $1.2k/month (reserved delta) vs. increasing batch duration — depends on traffic shape. For tonight's traffic, extending batch windows increases token-cost by ~8% on estimated jobs. Retirement looks cheaper for sustained wear.

infra-oncall: +1 for proactive retirement, but recommend canary retire first one node (gnode-57a), verify attach latencies and error rate for 1h, then proceed. Also open vendor SR for possible firmware wear pattern.

maria: Plan: 1) Canary retire gnode-57a now (drain ephemeral, move cached KV to next-hot node), 2) update attach-backoff policy: backoff multiplier -> x2 for 30m; 3) schedule full retire of 57b/57c tomorrow if remap_rate doesn't drop.

sophia: For the drain job, add a small delay to avoid evict storms: set concurrency=4 and slot_delay=6s. That should keep local-disk IOPS within headroom.

maria: Running drain now: `kubectl annotate node gnode-57a action=drain-proactive && ./drain-tool --node gnode-57a --concurrency 4 --slot-delay 6s`

devops-bot: JOB: drain-tool started for gnode-57a (job id: drain-3187654321-01). Estimated complete: 16m.

ajay: I'll watch attach metrics and adjust autoscaler buffer. If we see error tail after canary, we'll trigger rolling retire.

leo: I'll surface a short note to capacity planning: we may need to top-up ephemeral capacity in us-west2 next week if more nodes hit threshold.

maria: Action items: maria -> finish canary and post results; leo -> cost/impact note; ajay -> autoscaler buffer and alert tuning; infra-oncall -> open vendor SR and increase nvme-wear alarm sensitivity.

sophia: :thumbsup: Also flag postmortem template if retire crosses 5 nodes in 24h.

maria: Update: canary drain completed, attach retry rate dropped from 0.9% -> 0.15% in 12m, await on nvme0n1 on remaining nodes stable. Holding on full retire for now; keeping alert thresholds tighter. Will close thread after vendor SR ack or 24h stability.
